This Vice article is filled with fallacies.

A majority of the budget is spent on social programs, a large portion of the recipients are low earners.

Military spending is at ~3% of GDP which is REQUIRED by our NATO obligations.

"Creative accounting practices" isn't that creative. A company that pays an effective tax rate of zero even on a year with high profits is probably due to depreciation of assets or losses carried forward from previous years. Many American citizens who are landlords know that with depreciation, you can technically make a net profit on your rental income after expenses but show a loss after depreciation is taken into account. It's completely legal and millions do it, not just companies.

I don't agree with the high military spending or the amount of foreign aid we give. But citing "not wanting to fund wars" is intellectually dishonest. Especially since everyone takes advantage of one of the myriad of other services offered by taxes: K-12 schooling, public roads/highways, police, fire department, subsidized healthcare, welfare, EITC, to name a few.

If you don't want to pay federal income taxes, move to a country that have a high rate of tax evaders and tell me what you find there.
